rows.speaker: İbn Abbas, Dahhâk, Hasan, Katâde
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda are reported to prefer reading nūn as an inkpot.
rows.anchor: Yine İbn Abbas’tan mervî ve Dahhâk ve Hasan ve Katâde’nin muhtârı olarak bazıları da burada “nûn” devat

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye ve Râzî
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Rāzī cite an anonymous poet’s use of nūn as evidence for the sense “inkpot.”
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye ve Râzî bir şâirin şu beytiyle de istişhad eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the inkpot reading, the oath is by inkpot and pen because writing is done with them; books and writing are highly important and useful, though the pen alone conveys this too.
rows.anchor: Çünkü yazı bunlarla yazılır. Nutuk gibi kitab

rows.speaker: Muâviye b. Kurre
rows.claim: Muʿāwiya b. Qurra is said to transmit as a Prophetic report that nūn is a tablet of light.
rows.anchor: Muâviye b. Kurre’nin bunu bir hadîs-i merfû‘olarak naklettiği zikrolunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı suggests the light-tablet image may derive from the sun or earth appearing as a n-shaped point in the sky’s arc.
rows.anchor: Bu mâna; ufukta semâ kavsi içinde bir nokta gibi bulunan Güneş’in veya Arz’ın bir ن şekli resmetmesinden müste‘âr olabilir

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to identify nūn as the final letter of the name al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: Yine İbn Abbas’tan: اَل َّرحْمٰنُ harflerinin son harfidir

rows.speaker: Ca‘fer-i Sâdık
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq is reported to say that nūn is a river in Paradise.
rows.anchor: Ca‘fer-i Sâdık Hazretleri’nden: Cennet nehirlerinden bir nehirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon also gives nūn as inkpot, fish, sword-edge, a fish-shaped sword, a correct word, and the dimple in an infant’s chin (nūna).
rows.anchor: Kāmûs’ta mezkur olduğu üzere “nûn” devat ve hût mânasına geldiği gibi şefretü’s-seyf, yani kılıcın ağzına da denir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the feminine suffix marks singularity, nūn can be a generic noun for sword and the oath could be by sword and pen, although no report supports this reading here.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde “nûn” ism-i cins olarak نٓ وَٱلْقَلَمِ kılıç ve kaleme kasem olmak da muhtemildir. Lâkin burada buna dair bir rivayet vârid olmamıştır

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: The Kashshāf author takes nūn as an alphabetic letter: if it were a noun, its case and tanwīn or proper-name inflection would be missing, and its syntactic role unexplained; fish, tablet, and river readings face the same problem.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf demiştir ki: “Murad, hurûf-i mu‘cemden olan bu ن harfidir. Divit demelerine gelince, vaz‘-ı lügavî midir, yoksa şer‘î midir bilmem.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas ve Mücâhid
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid are cited for identifying nūn as the name of the great whale.
rows.anchor: Onun hût-i a‘zamın ismi olduğuna dair İbn Abbas ve Mücâhid’den

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyan
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān regards nūn as an ungoverned disjoint letter like ṣād and qāf, and says the transmitted identifications as whale, inkpot, tablet, al-Raḥmān’s last letter, or heavenly river are likely unsound.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyan da demiştir ki: “ن hurûf-i mu‘cemeden ص, ق gibi bir harftir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Nasr Abdurrahîm Kuşeyrî
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī likewise says nūn is an alphabetic initial: if it were a complete word it would inflect like qalam, as do other sūra openings.
rows.anchor: Ebû Nasr Abdurrahîm Kuşeyrî de tefsirinde; ن hurûf-i mu‘cemeden bir harftir. Tam bir kelime olsaydı ‘kalem’ gibi i‘rab olunurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı concludes that nūn is simply an alphabetic letter in writing and pronunciation, named as in reciting alif-bā; its basic function is challenge and testing the deeply rooted.
rows.anchor: Bizim bütün bunlardan vâsıl olduğumuz netice de şudur: Evet, resm-i hat ve lafız nokta-i nazarından burada ن sade bir hecâ harfidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being a letter does not prevent nūn from naming the sūra or serving as an ambiguous symbol that rationally suggests multiple meanings.
rows.anchor: Lâkin böyle olması sûrenin ismi olmasına mâni‘olmayacağı gibi, birçok mânalara delâlet-i akliye ile muhtemil müteşabih bir remz olmasını da mâni‘değil, muktezîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should not insist that a single possible sense is the intended one; reports about familiar meanings should not be rejected when they are not very weak and have intelligible, useful interpretations.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı “nûn” lafzının zihinleri sürükleyebileceği muhtemil mânalardan birini “murad budur” diyerek hasra kalkışmak doğru olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reads Ibn ʿAbbās’s multiple reports as separate possible aspects, each offered with a benefit, rather than as mutually exclusive claims to the sole intended meaning.
rows.anchor: Zira İbn Abbas’tan rivayetlerin ta‘addüdü gösteriyor ki o onları tahsis için birer vech olmak üzere söylemiş ve her birinde bir fâide beyan eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says to recall reports about the first-created pen when considering nūn, yet its intended sense remains among the ambiguous matters whose interpretation only God knows (3:7).
rows.anchor: أَ َّولُ مَا خَلَقَ االلهُ الْقَلَمَ fıkrası ve şu hâlde nûn sesinden hatıra gelebilen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the recitation makes nūn’s literal identity as a disjoint letter certain, this does not remove ambiguity: its relation to pen and writing must be inferred, making it a symbol with further possible senses.
rows.anchor: Lâkin burada bu kadarı teşabühün ref‘i için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It cannot be determined whether nūn itself contains an oath; if it does, the wāw before al-qalam is oath wāw, while the wāw before mā is connective.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde ن bir kasemi tazammun ediyor mu etmiyor mu kestirilemez. Kasem mukadder ise {وَٱلْقَلَمِ}deki vâv, وَمَا’deki gibi atıf için değil ise kasem için olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators give two analyses of al-qalam: the definite article may mark a particular known pen (ʿahd) or the genus of pens.
rows.anchor: Müfessirîn burada iki vecih söylemişlerdir. Birisi “lâm”ın ahd

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr identifies the known pen as the one God created and commanded to write what would occur through the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr der ki: “‘Kalem’, mâruf olan kalemdir. Şu kadar ki Rabbimizin kalemler içinde kasem ettiği kalem o kalemdir ki Teâlâ zikruhu halkedip emretmiştir

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that God first created the Pen and ordered it to write the decree, which it recorded for all that had happened and would happen forever; ʿUbāda’s deathbed counsel to his son stresses faith in good and bad destiny.
rows.anchor: Ben Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri’ni dinledim, diyordu ki: إ َّن أ َّولَ مَا خَلَقَ االلهُ خَلَقَ القَلَمَ فَقالَ لَهُ: اكْتُبْ

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses “nūn and the Pen” as that by which remembrance is written.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den de نٓ وَٱلْقَلَمِ kendisiyle zikir yazılandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı concludes that the referential Pen is the one that writes the Preserved Tablet or the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: Demek ki kasem olunan kalem şer‘an ma‘hud olan kalemdir ki o da Levh-i Mahfûz’u yazan kalem yahut Kur’an yazılan kalemdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other commentators take al-qalam generically, as in “taught by the pen” (96:4).
rows.anchor: olduğu gibi cinse hamledenler de vardır.

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: The Kashshāf says the oath honors the Pen because its creation and design display immense wisdom and its benefits exceed description.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf şöyle der: “Kaleme kasem buyurdu, şânına tâzim için, çünkü onun halk ve tesviyesinde hikmet-i azîmeye delâlet vardır

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says those who identify nūn as Behmūt take the Pen to be the cosmic pen God created and commanded to write the universe, with yasturun’s pronoun referring to angels.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye de demiştir ki

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explicitly identifies the subject of yasturun as people when the Pen means the familiar human writing tool.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas bunu tansis eylemiş ve يَسْطُرُونَ’daki zamiri de ‘nâs’a göndermiştir

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats the oath as covering writing as a whole, the foundation of knowledge and worldly and afterlife affairs; the Pen is the tongue’s sibling and a universal divine gift.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye de demiştir ki

rows.speaker: İmâm Râzî
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī’s generic reading includes pens used in heaven and earth: God’s gifts of speech and writing (55:3–4; 96:3–5) let people communicate beyond those nearby.
rows.anchor: İmâm Râzî de şöyle der: “‘Ve’l-kalem’de iki kavil vardır, birisi budur ki kasem edilen kalem, gerek semâda bulunanın ve gerek Arz’da bulunanın yazdığı kalemin hepsine vâki‘olan cinstir

rows.speaker: İmâm Râzî
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī’s second view is the particular first-created Pen, a luminous pen stretching between heaven and earth that writes events, lifespans, and deeds until the Hour.
rows.anchor: ma‘hud kalemdir. Allah teâlâ bunu evvelâ halketmiş, sonra da ona kıyamete kadar olacağı

rows.speaker: Kādî (Ebû Bekr Bâkıllânî olmalı)
rows.claim: The Qāḍī, probably Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī, reads the command to the Pen metaphorically: a writing tool is not a living, accountable intellect, so “write” means God brings events about by effective power, as in 2:117.
rows.anchor: Kādî (Ebû Bekr Bâkıllânî olmalı) demiştir ki: ‘Bu haberi mecâza hamletmek îcab eder. Çünkü kitabette âlet-i mahsûsa olan kalem emr ü nehy olunacak hay ve âkıl değildir

rows.speaker: İmâm Râzî
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī reports the claim that the Pen is intellect, the source of creatures: reports naming the first creation as Pen, intellect, or a primordial substance are reconciled as describing one thing.
rows.anchor: Yine Râzî der ki: “Nâstan bazı kimseler de şu zu‘mda bulunmuştur: Burada mezkur olan kalem akıldır.

rows.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī summarizes al-qalam as either the writer of the Tablet or the instrument used for writing; it is sworn by because its benefits are numerous.
rows.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî de bunları şöyle hulâsa eder: “Ve’l-kalem, Levh’i yazan, yahut kendisiyle yazılandır. Ona kasem buyuruldu. Çünkü fevâidi çoktur

rows.speaker: Suyûtî
rows.claim: Al-Jalālayn says the Pen is that by which the universe was written on the Preserved Tablet; Elmalılı says al-qalam could sound generic, but al-Suyūṭī intends a particular known Pen.
rows.anchor: Tefsîr-i Celâleyn’de de der ki: “Kalem kâinâtın Levh-i Mahfuz’da yazıldığıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particular Pen also belongs to the genus; the familiar human pen taught in 96:4 is the plain example, and human writing has recorded thought and memory from creation onward and will continue.
rows.anchor: Mâlum ki ma‘hud da cins cümlesindendir. عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ mısdâkınca insana tâlim olunan cins-i kalemden zâhir olan ise mâlumumuz olan kalem-i beşer görünür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when the oath refers to one particular Pen, it honors the genus of pens and therefore also gives dignity to the human pen.
rows.anchor: gerek hakikat gerek mecaz her ne mâna ile olursa olsun kaleme kasem edilince bundan bir ferd-i ma‘hud

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a general audience, the human pen would be the apparent sense, as in 96:4–5; under a particular reference, one or several pens may be intended, and metaphor may point to the primordial pen of nature.
rows.anchor: Eğer bu kasemin cevâbında muhatab bilhassa Hazret-i Peygamber’in kendisi olmasaydı da hitâb-ı âm olsa idi, burada عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ عَلَّمَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ [el-Alâk 96/4-5] gibi kalem-i beşer murad olunmak zâhir olurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the address is specifically to Muḥammad, recipient of divine favor and noble character, who neither read nor wrote before revelation nor knew the Book (29:48; 42:52), Elmalılı prefers the divine primordial Pen, also called the First or Highest Pen; he finds this view in Ibn Jarīr and al-Jalālayn.
rows.anchor: Fakat burada hitab bilhassa ni‘met-i ilâhiyeye mazhar kılınarak, وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍۢ [el-Kalem 68/4] buyurulan zât-ı Hazret-i Muhammedî’ye ait olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In uṣūl terms, al-qalam explicitly denotes the divine Pen and indicates the human pen by implication; those saying “genus” encompass both literal and metaphorical senses but do not distinguish explicit text from apparent indication.
rows.anchor: Bu وَٱلْقَلَمِ’de “kalem”, kalem-i ilâhîde bi’l-ibâre nas, dolayısıyla kalem-i beşer hakkında da bi’l-işâre zâhir demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article is not exhaustive: the oath does not honor every pen, and Elmalılı says no commentator takes it as alif-lām of total inclusion.
rows.anchor: Sonra şunu da unutmamak lâzım gelir ki bu وَٱلْقَلَمِ’de elif lâmın istiğrak için olduğuna kāil olan yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pens used to falsify truth, harm God’s servants, and spread discord through malice, immorality, or stupidity are pens but deserve no praise for truth and goodness.
rows.anchor: Zira hakkı ibtal veya ibâdullahı ızrar yolunda şeytanet ve ahlâksızlık veya idraksizlikle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following denial of madness, affirmation of divine favor, understanding, character, and great reward, and condemnation of immoral liars clarify which side of the pen’s significance is praised.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı burada bu kasemin arkasından cünûnun, fitnenin nefyi ve ni‘met-i rabbâniyenin idrak ve ahlâkın, ecrin büyüklüğünü beyan ve ahlâksızların, yalancıların zemmi ile o cihete de tenbih buyurulacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı’s rendering addresses Muḥammad: pause over the opening called Nūn; he swears by it, the known Pen of Truth, and what the people of the Pen have written and will write.
rows.anchor: ve ehl-i kalemin satıra dizip yazdıklarına ve yazacaklarına ki yâ Muhammed!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasturun is a sound masculine plural, normally used for rational beings; attributing writing to an unmentioned rational plural behind the singular Pen points to its unseen intelligent users as the real writers.
rows.anchor: “Kalem” müfred olarak zikrolunduğu hâlde yazış ve yazılanlar ona nisbet edilmeyip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible tool signifies its hidden rational user; the Pen stands for the writing it produces, and the connective wāw joins an oath encompassing the Pen, writings, and their intelligent authors.
rows.anchor: “Kalem”den maksud da kendisi değil, o yazdıklarıdır, وَمَا,وَٱلْقَلَمِ’daki vâv-ı atıf gibi bir âlettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From pen and writing one should infer the world of intellects and meanings, then the First Pen that writes them into human intellect, and finally its Lord, the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle burada vâv atıf için olarak kasem, kalem ve yazılarıyla sâhipleri olan ehl-i idrâke delâlet etmek üzere mecmû‘una yapılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the human Pen, its writers are rational people—consciousness and intelligence rather than visible bodies; for the Highest Pen, angels write forms of things and meanings, while God writes them.
rows.anchor: Kalem-i beşere nazaran yazıcılar ehl-i kalem, akıl ve idrak sâhibi insanlar, hem de göze görünen bedenler değil, insanlık hakikatini teşkil eden şuurlar, zekâlar olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in yasturun can refer to human writers with the human Pen or to angels with the Highest Pen, explaining why commentaries give either “people” or “angels.”
rows.anchor: Bunun için burada وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ’un fâili olan zamir kalem-i beşere nazaran müdrik insanlara işaret olduğu gibi, Kalem-i A‘lâ’ya nazaran da melâike olmak üzere tefsir edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turkish lacks the sound masculine plural form, so “the Pen and what they write” does not express the shift from the instrument to its intelligent users.
rows.anchor: Lisânımızda böyle cem‘-i müzekker-i sâlim sîgası bulunmadığı için bu nükte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasturun is imperfective and indicates continuity into the present and future; Turkish translations cannot capture all of this tense and aspect nuance.
rows.anchor: Bir de يَسْطُرُونَ muzâri‘sîgasıdır. İstimrâra ve hâl ü istikbâle delâlet eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Highest Pen was active when these verses descended and continues to write; the report that the Pen has dried means what has occurred is written, not that writing of future events has ceased.
rows.anchor: Bu bize şunu da anlatmış oluyorki bu âyetler nâzil olurken Kalem-i A‘lâ cereyan ediyordu ve daha edecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete finality in decree pertains to God’s knowledge, the Mother of the Book; with respect to the Preserved Tablet and created existence, God erases and establishes (13:39).
rows.anchor: Kaderde ferâğ-ı tâm Ümmü’l-Kitâb olan ilmullâha nazarandır. Yoksa Levh-i Mahfûz’a ve sâha-i tekvîne nazaran يَمْحُوا۟ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيُثْبِتُ’dir [er-Ra‘d 13/39]
